Such voltage saturation can result in excessive current spikes which can damage sensitive equipment and shorten transformer life. Some common methods of mitigating or blocking the ef- fects of CM are as follows: (a) adding passive blocking devices [5], (b) im- plementing corrective line switching [6], (c) using active devices to disrupt geomagnetically induced currents (GICs) in the transformer neutral [7], and (d) utilizing power electronics converters that can respond to and counteract CM insults [8, 9]. This paper focuses on the aforementioned option (d). The work presented in this paper focuses on designing a power electronics-based controller which can rapidly mitigate CM insults on the grid. Particularly, this paper focuses on annihilation of offset in phase currents which has been induced by a CM insult. The proposed control scheme presented in this paper is intended to be utilized to control the output inverter of an SST. SSTs have been proposed as a solution to allow for more efficient, autonomous control of power flow [10]. Additionally, distributed energy resources (DERs) are being integrated into the grid more widely due to increased environmental, climate, and na- tional security concerns. These DERs include solar (photovoltaic) energy, wind energy, wave energy, and energy storage. Because these types of energy sources are either DC in nature or operate at a frequency differing from that of the main grid, a power electronics interface (PEI) must be used to couple them to the main grid. For these sources to be optimally utilized, smart control is a necessity [11]. In this paper, the control design for a 4-leg inverter stage that can be used in SST technologies or as an independent converter is developed. The proposed control scheme uses the topology of the SST proposed in [9]. In 2 [9], simulations were used to demonstrate the SST’s capability of effectively responding to CM insults. In [12], a Hamiltonian control method was intro- duced to improve controller response.
